A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations, transformer eigenvalue experiments and XLSUM summarization results, including additional fine-tuning experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original results in all three settings and reports additional noisy-verifier experiments and empirical proxy measurements.

M1.justification: The learning models, objectives and basic verifier-based pruning procedure are retained. Verification-pruning renames RLHF-pruning; the noisy-verifier experiments instantiate the existing pruning family, while the proxy assesses verifier quality without introducing a new training algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gaussian-mixture classification, eigenvalue prediction for uniformly sampled 5×5 symmetric matrices, and English XLSUM summarization. The additional experiments vary verification and sample sizes within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: The revised arithmetic comparison introduces controlled noisy verifiers alongside oracle and unselected-data controls. Oracle beam-label selection remains in Appendix B.1. The summarization comparator set is unchanged: oracle, Llama-3, self-selection, random selection, generator and full-original-data references.

E3.justification: The main arithmetic study changes from beam/rejection comparisons and a 12M-sample tolerance study to verifier-noise sweeps evaluated at 1% tolerance with 1M, 5M and 10M samples. Simulation pruner angles change from π/12 and π/6 to π/24 and π/12. V2 also measures the verifier-quality proxy across experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds systematic sensitivity to verifier noise and examines the relationship between the proxy and performance in simulations, arithmetic and summarization. The earlier 12M stricter-tolerance ablation is removed. The appendix analysis comparing fine-tuning different pretrained models with training from scratch is retained.

E5.justification: V1 reports the best of five seeds for Table 2; v2 Figure 4 reports five-seed averages with error bars. This changes aggregation and uncertainty reporting without establishing an increased run count. The meaning of the new error bars is unspecified.

E6.justification: V2 adds noisy-verifier accuracy curves, measured proxy values, additional Llama-3 curve points at 25% and 50% selection, and the verifier's ROUGE-1 score of 34.5. V1's 12M results and Table 2's 1%/0.5% results disappear. Table 1 and Appendix B.1 values remain. The new arithmetic results do not establish like-for-like performance gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix C formally extends p, φ and ψ from binary correctness to similarity scores in [0,1], enabling the ROUGE-based proxy. The original breakdown-point theorem, assumptions, derivations and proofs remain substantively unchanged in the renumbered theory appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion make a measurable proxy that predicts downstream performance a central contribution. V2 also drops the abstract's assertion that the findings validate popular approaches such as RLHF. The underlying claim that suitable selection can prevent model collapse remains.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds an explanation of self-improvement through selecting new inputs and changing their distribution, distinguishing this from selecting labels for fixed inputs. V2 recommends proxy-guided verifier choice and interprets the arithmetic crossover as a phase transition. The explicit limitation concerning untested prompt engineering is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies that the Llama-3 verifier was fine-tuned on the full XLSUM dataset. Appendix B generalizes the 400-epoch training statement and removes the 12M-specific runtime estimate. Most architecture, optimization, hardware, preprocessing and resource-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds comparisons with synthetic-data correction, detection and negative-guidance work, including Gillman, Zhang and Alemohammad, plus verifier applications by Setlur and Ulmer. It explicitly positions the contribution as analyzing selection rather than proposing new selection algorithms. The extensive Appendix A taxonomy remains.

P1.justification: The title changes from reinforcement to verification, with extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, related work and experimental narrative. The former Section 5.1 becomes an expanded warmup before the theory, and a new proxy appendix changes the subsequent appendix organization.

P2.justification: V2 adds proxy bar-chart rows to the simulation and summarization figures, introduces the arithmetic noise-response figure and an experiment-overview table, and removes the earlier main arithmetic result tables. Table 1 moves into the warmup, and typography, headers and figure arrangements change throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful proxy diagnostics, noisy-verifier tests and five-seed averages. However, Figure 4 uses a generator baseline around 31% at 1% tolerance, while retained Table 1 reports 20.2%, without explaining whether a different generator was used. This ambiguity affects the new model-collapse and phase-transition validation, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
